title: A comment on Leal et al.: ‘Geometric morphometrics reveal that Conus anabathrum Crosse, 1865 (Neogastropoda:Conidae) should be an accepted species’
content: This paper examines the shifts in taxonomy and roles that the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN) have played in the debate of Gradiconus anabathrum being synonymized with either Gradiconus floridanus or Gradiconus scalaris. Gradiconus anabathrum (Crosse, 1865) has been an enigma for taxonomists for over 100 years primarily due to the failure of Crosse to designate a type locality, and the location of a population of organisms that is congruent. Notwithstanding, the holotype of C. anabathrum is clearly identifiable from the collection of Hugh Cuming held at the Natural History Museum, London, UK. Nevertheless, in spite of Gradiconus anabathrum being considered a lost species by Tomlin (1937) and Wagner & Abbott (1964), in 1980 Coomans declared that Gradiconus anabathrum was synonymous with Gradiconus floridanus (Gabb, 1869) (Coomans, Moolenbeek & Wils 1980).
